messages:
ella_infra: FYI — EU-west started backfilling dedicated overflow to shared pools at 09:12 UTC, lots of small preemptible jobs spilled.
sam_ops: noticed a latency tail and a few failed init handshakes around that time. error rate +4.3% on dedicated slices.
rohit: digging logs. seeing a cluster of short-lived micro-batches that align with tenant spike. kernel boot churn + KV cache misses. snippet:
```
WARN 09:12:34 preempt: tenant=acme job=tx-342 preempt_by=spot-drain
INFO 09:12:35 kvcache: miss tenant=acme key=ctx-abc
ERR 09:12:35 socket: connection reset by peer
```
kai: is this the warm-pool prefetch we tuned last week? if warm pool isn't populated the small bursts hit cold paths and cause IO spikes.
ella_infra: yes — looks like warm pool warmup failed for eu-west-2b because capacity was donated to a regional batch window.
sam_ops: consequence: dedicated tenants see noisy-neighbor shimmer from shared pods that picked up backfill. throughput jitter = high percentiles.
cost-ops: cost note — cross-region backfill increased preemptible egress and re-provision churn, added ~8% to hourly GPU cost in that AZ.
rohit: hypothesis: our fallthrough routing prefers any-available which sent a lot of short jobs into dedicated slices rather than routing them to a separated shared-spot pool. need to bias routing by duration_estimate and tenant_qos.
kai: quick mitigation proposal:
- lower fallthrough weight for dedicated pools by 0.6
- route <30s estimated jobs to dedicated-shared-spot pool only
- ensure warm-pool grace of 90s for eu-west
ella_infra: + add a fastpath that checks kvcache warm state before accepting spillback to dedicated slices.
sam_ops: operational playbook steps:
1) pause cross-region batch windows for 15m (we already signaled job-scheduler)
2) increase dedicated fallback cooldown to 120s
3) drain and reprovision one warm pool shard in eu-west-2b
rohit: command I ran to surface affected tenants:
```
./bin/spot-inspect --region eu-west-2 --since 09:00 --filter preempt=true --fields tenant,job,duration_est
```
kai: after the changes I see successful stabilization in canary cluster: p99 latency dropped from 540ms -> 220ms for affected routes.
cost-ops: anticipate short-term cost bump from reprovisioning (~$600/hr) but avoids SLA penalties for key customers.
ella_infra: long term: consider a routing hedging policy that reserves a 5-10% preemptible-only pool in each region to absorb batch spikes without touching dedicated pools.
rohit: agree. plus telemetry: add a warm-pool occupancy metric and a preempt-spillback-counter so we can alert before degradation.
infra-bot: incident note created: INC-2026-0432 "eu-west warm-pool backfill ripple". Pager alert suppressed (low severity), runbook link: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/warm-pool-backfill
sam_ops: Triage owners: @ella_infra, @rohit. I'll monitor for next 2 hours.
kai: leaving a followup PR to routing weights: PR #4532 -> set fallthrough_weight=0.4 for dedicated in eu-west, add duration cutover.
ella_infra: thanks all. please add any tenants you saw impacted to the incident thread so we can notify account owners.
sam_ops: adding acme-inc and fastforms to the list.
rohit: tracking: put a task to run a simulation against synthetic short-batch traces to validate policy before global rollout.
ella_infra: ack — will coordinate with infra-test to run simulation tomorrow morning.
sam_ops: closing loop if no regressions in 2h we keep changes and schedule a 72h observation window. :thumbsup:
